text:
julia.product: Drafting the Dedicated Capacity PRD — need quick alignment on SLA targets, throughput sizing, and autoscale rules. Sharing a short proposal below, please react or reply with objections.

mike.eng-platform: +1, drop the doc link?

julia.product: https://redwood.internal/docs/prd/dedicated-capacity-v1 (draft) — tl;dr: aim for enterprise-grade guarantees customers asked for: consistent throughput, predictable latency, and controlled autoscale.

sam.sre: Quick Q: are we committing to hard p99 or p50 for the SLA? Customers often expect p99.

julia.product: Proposal: p99 tail latency for inference endpoint <= 200ms for short chat requests (<=256 tokens), p99 <= 500ms for longer sequences (<=2048 tokens). Availability SLA 99.95% monthly. If that feels unrealistic we can scope to 99.9% for GA and tighten later.

mike.eng-platform: 200ms p99 for <=256 is borderline but achievable on A100s with optimized kernel selection + warm cache. We need acceptance criteria and telemetry to prove it. Also define measurement windows and traffic profile.

nina.pmo: Acceptance criteria suggestion (short):
- Latency: p99 within target for 14 days under customer workload simulation (see load profile).
- Throughput: sustained throughput >= committed RPS per dedicated pool size with <1% request queueing.
- Failover: automatic fallback to a lower-cost model variant with documented behavior on node failures.
- Observability: per-tenant dashboards and SLO alerts wired to incidents team.

carla.sales: Customers asking for committed throughput tiers: small=200k tokens/min, medium=1M tokens/min, large=5M tokens/min. They want linear scaling for extra units and clear overage behavior.

mike.eng-platform: OK for tiers. Need to map tokens/min to concurrent requests and GPU sizing. Rough mapping I'm using:
```
small (N-1 GPU): 1 x 3090 or 1 x A10 equivalent -> ~150 concurrent short-chat sessions
medium: 4 x A100s -> ~700 concurrent
large: 16 x A100s -> ~3000 concurrent
```
These are rough; we'll run perf bench to validate.

sam.sre: Autoscaling rules: customers expect predictable latency during spikes. Proposal: reserved baseline capacity + burst pool with 60s scale-up target and 10m scale-down to avoid flapping. Also an emergency manual scale override for SRE/SE.

julia.product: That aligns with ask. Two policy options for GA: (A) instantish autoscale (60s) with capped burst (recommended), (B) scheduled scaling with warm-up for high-SLA customers. Need to pick one for initial scope.

carla.sales: For sales deals, they will pay for scheduled warm capacity. So (B) could be a paid add-on, but default should be (A).

nina.pmo: Launch criteria proposal:
- Technical: Benchmarks against target traffic profiles (stable p99 for 14-day sim).
- Support: On-call runbook + escalation paths, documented fallbacks.
- Legal/Commercial: SLA SLO language + overage billing in contract template.
- UX: Console controls for pool sizing, schedule, and real-time metrics.

mike.eng-platform: Edge cases we should list in PRD:
- Partial node failure during a canary rollout -> ensure split traffic and deterministic fallback.
- Cold-start for large models (seq>1024) leading to transient p99 spikes -> mitigate via pre-warming and cache priming.
- Multi-tenant noisy neighbor on shared burst pool -> isolate via token-rate caps and per-tenant queue priority.
- Model upgrade rollback within 1 minute for critical regressions.

sam.sre: Add SLO burn-rate thresholds and automated remediation runbooks (eg. auto-routing to secondary region if burn rate >5x for 5min).

julia.product: Acceptance criteria to include tests and tooling:
- Perf harness: synthetic + customer replay that covers 10 distinct traffic shapes.
- Regression tests for cold-starts using long-context sequences.
- Chaos tests for node/network failure.

carla.sales: Customers also ask for clear SLA credits formula. We should include a simple table: <99.95% -> 5% credit, <99.9% -> 10% credit. Legal can tweak.

nina.pmo: Scope negotiation: For GA we limit model family to LlamaX-variants and GPT-compat models that we've optimized kernels for. Wider model catalog can be on roadmap post-GA. Keep deployment regions to us-west-2 and eu-west-1 initially.

mike.eng-platform: Implementation notes: need autoscaler (controller) + pool manager + admission controller that enforces queueing and priority. Also a rollout planner for canary + metric gating. SRE to own remediate playbooks.

sam.sre: For metrics, we must emit per-tenant p50/p95/p99, request queue length, per-GPU utilization, and token/sec. Instrument at ingress and runtime.

julia.product: Next steps: mike to post perf bench plan & target mapping, sam to draft SLO runbooks, nina to consolidate commercial SLA language, carla to flag any big customer asks. I'll update PRD with chosen SLA numbers and GA scope by EOD Friday.

deploy-bot: deploy pipeline: prd/dedicated-capacity-v1 updated by julia.product at 1711004823.

mike.eng-platform: ACK — will start running perf sweeps tomorrow and ping results here.

carla.sales: 👍 will coordinate customer pilots once we have medium tier benchmarks.

julia.product: Thanks all — short sync tomorrow 10am to lock on final numbers.
